title: Ingest deduper and contract compatibility layer for event spikes
creator: Jonah Kim
description: Problem: during sudden client spikes and replay scenarios our usage event pipeline sees duplicate and near-duplicate envelopes which inflate costs, pollute dashboards, and trigger false regressions in quality checks. This ticket implements a two-part mitigation: (1) a lightweight deduplication preprocessor in the ingest proxy that detects identical or near-identical events within a sliding window and drops/marks duplicates; (2) a contract compatibility shim that accepts older event shapes and upgrades them to the canonical schema at ingest time rather than dropping them. Scope: engine-level dedup logic (memory-efficient fingerprinting + TTL), config-driven duplicate actions (drop/mark/route-to-async), and a compatibility layer for a defined set of legacy fields used by older SDKs. Out of scope: full schema evolution framework, long-term storage migration, and UI changes to console dashboards (those are separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Ingest proxy rejects or marks >90% exact duplicate events within a 60s window without increasing p95 latency by >12ms
Compatibility shim transforms legacy payloads to canonical schema for at least three known legacy variants documented in Confluence
Backend metrics: deduped_events, dedup_false_positive_rate <1%, dropped_events_derating logged
End-to-end test: synthetic replay of 10k duplicate events results in <=1.1x ingestion cost relative to baseline (no spike) due to dedupe and backpressure
Instrumentation: PR includes dashboard links and tracing spans showing dedupe decision and transform path
notes: Design decision: use Murmur3 128-bit fingerprint + sliding TTL keyed by customer+route to avoid cross-tenant dedupe collisions
Tradeoff: in-memory LRU vs Redis TTL set. Started with in-memory for latency but added Redis path for Dedicated deployments where memory footprint is constrained
Privacy: fingerprints are derived from stable event signature fields (no raw PII), documented in security review notes
Fallback behavior: when Redis is unavailable, system falls back to probabilistic Bloom filter to avoid unbounded memory growth
We will not attempt semantic deduping (near-duplicate NLP similarity) in this ticket; that would be a follow-up research spike
timeline: Week 1: design + PoC fingerprinting in local ingest-proxy; Week 2: add Redis optional path and compatibility transforms; Week 3: integration tests, load tests, and dashboarding; Week 4: production canary rollout to 10% traffic then ramp
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Observability and SDK teams. Agreed canonical field set and TTL defaults (60s for exact, 300s for inferred session keys).
2025-02-20: PoC committed — local benchmark shows dedupe path adds 6ms median and 9ms p95. Decided acceptable; will optimize for p95 in next iteration.
2025-02-24: Integration tests added for three legacy payload variants. One variant required a small transform for renamed fields; added mapping table.

2025-02-28: Load test with synthetic 50k events/sec burst in k8s staging. Redis backed dedupe held; in-memory fallback showed memory pressure on small instance types. Plan to gate in-memory on instance size.
2025-03-01: Draft PR opened for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/1347. Seeking review from @sasha and @anil for correctness and security.
2025-03-02: Security sign-off requested for fingerprint approach; privacy team asked to confirm field set used for hashing.
